applicant_utility.summary: This combined award is built specifically for underrepresented students: a Dutch grade equivalent of 8.0 is the academic bar, but belonging to a disadvantaged group and demonstrating community involvement carry equal weight. Only three research masters at Erasmus MC qualify, and the page warns that the eligible programmes change each academic year, so the award can exist for your programme one year and not the next. The file itself has hard formatting rules: every PDF must follow the studentnumber_lastname naming format, and the budget plan must use the provided template, so leave time to rename and reformat rather than uploading files at the deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving applicants to the Erasmus MC Research Masters in Health Sciences, Neuroscience or Molecular Medicine who belong to an underrepresented group and can evidence community involvement.

Prepare a separate motivation letter per scholarship if you apply to more than one
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a Research Master's programme that is not funded in the current year
An average below the equivalent of Dutch 8.0
Uploading an unformatted budget plan or misnamed PDFs
Failing to demonstrate community involvement and commitment to the Changemaker network, which is a stated requirement
Non-EEA applicants assuming eligibility where the page states EEA nationality
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award covers the statutory fee, living allowance and one year of housing, but non-EU/EEA institutional-fee payers receive only a partial waiver where applicable, so the institutional tuition gap and travel remain uncovered.

applicant_utility.summary: EUR 30,000 covers your Leiden tuition and the housing request fee, with the small remainder paid to you monthly, but Leiden is explicit: this is not a full scholarship, so you must independently fund rent, travel and the rest of your living costs and prove sufficient funds for your residence permit. Only one award is made per year to a student from the eighteen listed Arab countries, so the field is narrow but the competition within it is fierce. The application runs through the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation's own procedure rather than Leiden's scholarship system, and the window is a tight three months from 1 January to 31 March.
applicant_utility.best_fit: An exceptional student from one of the eighteen listed Arab countries with a Leiden one-year Master's admission (or entering year two of a two-year Master's) and a demonstrated commitment to Euro-Arab dialogue.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure your Leiden admission letter first; the scholarship application depends on it and late admission files are your own responsibility
Read the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation's published application requirements early, since they govern the file rather than Leiden's
Prepare proof of sufficient funds for the visa/residence permit that covers rent and living costs beyond the award
Budget for the English test yourself; it is a prerequisite of admission and is not reimbursed
Decide before 31 March whether to request housing via Leiden University, whose request fee the scholarship pays
common_rejection_risks: Nationality outside the eighteen listed countries
Applying to an LLM Advanced Studies programme, whose higher tuition fees this award does not cover
Submitting an incomplete Leiden admission application before the deadline; Leiden disclaims responsibility for late files
Underestimating the self-funding requirement for rent, travel and living costs, which leads to a residence-permit funds shortfall even after winning
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The rent itself (only the housing fee is covered), travel to the Netherlands, the remainder of living costs and the English test fee are all yours; the award explicitly does not cover all the recipient's expenses in the Netherlands.
document_audit: Second-year applicants to a two-year Master's must provide proof of enrolment in that second year, not a first-year admission letter
